# L-148 — A fix applied to a generated file has a half-life, and the gate that finds it is the next rebuild

Found 2026-08-30 in [T-257](../../tasks/T-257-ds-218-passes-the-shipped-example-vacuously.md),
which had to rebuild `portfolio-review` to give it a looping motion.
[T-233](../../tasks/T-233-a-shipped-deck-carries-eleven-copies-of-one-source.md) had removed ten
duplicated quick-view payloads from the built deck four days earlier, and
[L-147](L-147.md) records what that found. **It edited the `.html`. It did not edit
`tools/examples/portfolio_charts.py`, which writes the `.html`.** So the first rebuild after it put
all ten back, and `quickview.py check` reported `DUPLICATE` on a tree that had been green since the
day the fix landed.

**It happened three times in one rebuild, from two different tasks.** The duplication was
`T-233`'s. `T-248` had corrected slide 6's revaluation figure from `$131M` to `$102M` in three
places and retitled its disclosure, also in the built file - and the rebuild put all four back,
including a change **the owner had looked at and confirmed**
([`OWED-LOOKS.md`](../OWED-LOOKS.md) row 8). So the queue of owed looks was carrying a signed-off
answer to a question the tree had quietly re-opened.

**The second failure in the same run is the sharper one.** The builder rendered its own quick-view
markdown, and `quickview.py check` compares the template against the source using **its** renderer.
The two agreed on everything except emphasis - the builder left `*text*` literal where `render`
emits `<i>` - so the rebuilt deck reported `DRIFTED` at word 560 against a source document nobody
had touched. Neither tool was wrong; they were two renderers with one output to agree on, and
nothing made them agree.

- **A generated artifact has exactly one author, and it is not a person.** Fixing the artifact is
  fixing the output of a function without fixing the function: correct today, reverted the next time
  anybody runs it, and reverted *silently* unless something downstream happens to be watching.
- **The revert is invisible for as long as nobody rebuilds**, which is precisely how long the fix
  looks like it worked. Four days here, and it would have been longer - `REMEDIATION-ORDER.md`'s
  rule 3 rebuilds the decks **once**, in one batch, so the next rebuild after B12 was not scheduled
  at all. The fix's expiry date was *whenever someone next has a reason*.
- **Where two tools must produce the same bytes, one of them imports the other.** The builder now
  calls `quickview.render`, so the template it writes is the template the check compares by
  construction rather than by two implementations staying in step. That is
  [L-08](L-08.md) applied to a renderer, and it is the only version of *keep them in sync* that
  does not need anybody to remember.

**And a typed figure is the same fault one level down.** `$131M` was the sum of all three
revaluation lines where the slide claims the renewables ones, so the wrong number was *derivable
from the table printed beside it* and nobody derived it - it was typed in three places and
corrected in three places. It is now one constant summed from the table, and the builder's self-test
asserts it is not the three-line total. **A figure stated more than once has already chosen how it
will go wrong.**

**What to do with it.** When a fix lands in a file some command produces, the fix is not done until
the command produces it. Ask what wrote the file before editing it, and if the answer is a script,
change the script and re-run it - **then diff, because the rebuild carries everything else that has
drifted since the last one as well.** This rebuild did: it was the run that surfaced both faults,
and it also cost the deck 87,335 bytes it had been carrying back.
